content.title: About
content.content: Colby Jack cheese is an American semi‑hard cheese made from a blend of cow’s milk and sometimes goat’s milk. It combines the mild, buttery flavor of Colby with the smooth texture of Monterey Jack, resulting in a marbled orange‑yellow appearance and a slightly tangy aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Created in the early 20th century in California as a hybrid of Cheddar and Monterey Jack.
The orange hue is achieved with natural colorants such as paprika or annatto.
Commonly used in Mexican‑inspired dishes like fajitas and nachos.
Melts exceptionally well, making it popular for casseroles, grilled sandwiches, and burgers.
Often sold pre‑sliced for quick snack or sandwich use.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Provides a good amount of calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Source of high‑quality protein
items.content: Delivers complete dairy protein needed for tissue repair and growth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains B12, riboflavin and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Phosphorus and zinc
items.content: Contribute to immune function and metabolic processes.

items.title: Reduced lactose content
items.content: Aging breaks down some lactose, making it easier to tolerate for people with mild lactose sensitivity.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to dairy proteins may experience reactions ranging from hives to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: The cheese is salted, so those with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Its fat content makes it energy‑dense; moderation is key for weight management.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Excessive intake can affect cholesterol levels.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Colby Jack melts beautifully in sauces, casseroles, on pizza, and in burger patties. It can also be sliced for sandwiches, added to salads, or enjoyed as a snack with fruit and nuts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cheese in the refrigerator at 35‑40 °F (2‑4 °C), wrapped in parchment paper and then in a sealed container or plastic wrap. Properly stored, it stays fresh for 4‑6 weeks. Discard if you notice mold beyond the surface or an off‑smell.
